sources.citation: Samad, Musdelifa Abu, Yuslin Kasan, Mukhtar I. Miolo, Wiranto Talibo & Anggie Potale. 2025. Struktur Klausa Bahasa Arab dan Bahasa Andio: Analisis Kontrastif, Pelestarian Bahasa. 'A Jamiy: Jurnal Bahasa dan Sastra Arab (Universitas Muhammadiyah Gorontalo) 14(1): 123-139. doi:10.31314/ajamiy.14.1.123-139.2025
sources.note: No phonology content: contrastive description of nominal/verbal/transitive/intransitive/reflexive/reciprocal clauses with Andio example sentences in plain orthography (no diacritics). Notes a 1988 Andio folktale manuscript 'Kodo' Tibai Ree'a' by the late Arfat Bidja used by the Australian researcher 'Mr. Billy'. Reference list contains no other Andio work.

sources.citation: Sulawesi Language Alliance. Andio language page (sulang.org/languages/andio) and Word Lists / Phonology series pages; Internet Archive copy 2025-08-08 and 2025-01-26 (sulang.org itself unreachable 2026-09-17).
sources.note: No stress information. The Andio page cites only Barr & Barr 1979, Busenitz 1991 (lexicostatistic/sociolinguistic survey, pp. 1-17), Mead 2003 and Moseley 2010; the site's Phonology and Orthography series holds only Sangir and Kulisusu papers; the only Andio resource on the site is the 2013 word list above.

sources.citation: Andi-Pallawa, Baso. 2013. Function words of Andio language viewed from syntactical aspect. Academic Journal of Interdisciplinary Studies 2(2): 175-189. doi:10.5901/ajis.2013.v2n2p175 (Tadulako University).
sources.note: Nothing. Purely syntactic inventory of function words elicited from speakers in Tangeban and Taugi; no phonology, no stress or accent mention; its reference list contains no other work on Andio.

sources.citation: Busenitz, Robert L. 2013 [data collected August 1988]. Andio word list and sentences (eastern Sulawesi, Indonesia). Sulang Language Data and Working Papers: Word Lists, no. 2. Sulawesi Language Alliance (sulang.org). 22 pp. Public domain.
sources.note: Nothing. The one-page introduction explains only the apostrophe (glottal stop), digraph ng, and orthographic e; the 488-item word list and 44 elicited sentences carry no stress marks or diacritics of any kind, and stress is never mentioned. This is the only first-hand Andio language data found online.

sources.citation: Mead, David. 2003. The Saluan-Banggai microgroup of eastern Sulawesi. In John Lynch (ed.), Issues in Austronesian historical phonology (Pacific Linguistics 550), 65-86. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics. (Online edition 2015, CC BY-SA 4.0, via the SEAlang/CRCL Pacific Linguistics archive.)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent (the words do not occur; 'antepenultimate/penultimate' appear only in sound-change labels). Comparative sound-change paper on Saluan, Bobongko, Andio, Balantak, Banggai; its Andio data are Busenitz's 1988 word list (p.68 fn.). Only prosody-adjacent remark: lengthened vowels (from *y > -0-V:) 'were then lost as a drift-like tendency in Bobongko, Andio, and certain of the Saluan dialects' (printed p.78).

sources.citation: Busenitz, Robert L. 1991. Lexicostatistic and sociolinguistic survey of Balantak and Andio. In Timothy Friberg (ed.), UNHAS-SIL more Sulawesi sociolinguistic surveys, 1987-1991 (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 11), 1-17. Ujung Pandang: SIL.
sources.note: The only Andio-specific publication besides the word list; a survey report by the same fieldworker, may contain a brief phonological note. SIL archive copy likely exists (sil.org/resources/archives) but the site blocks automated access.

sources.citation: Noorduyn, J. 1991. The languages of Sulawesi. In H. Steinhauer (ed.), Papers in Austronesian linguistics No. 1 (Pacific Linguistics A-81), 137-150. Canberra: Research School of Pacific Studies, Australian National University. (ANU Open Research hdl 1885/253602, file, 14 pp.)
sources.note: Nothing on Andio stress or tone ('stress' occurs once, later in the paper, in the sense 'rightly stressed' = emphasised). Value for the bibliography: it fixes what exists on Andio as of 1991 -- two 100-word lists (Barr, Barr & Salombe 1979:102-104; Wumbu et al. 1983:135-138, the unpublished version of the 1986 Depdikbud inventory) -- so the still-unobtained Wumbu et al. 1986 is a wordlist for Andio, not a sketch; and it settles the Andi'o vs Bobongko identity (Wurm & Hattori atlas no.43 conflated them).

sources.citation: Barr, Donald F., Sharon G. Barr & C. Salombe. 1979. Languages of Central Sulawesi: checklist, preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Ujung Pandang: UNHAS-SIL. 109 pp.
sources.note: First recognition of Andio as a distinct language (p.36) with wordlists; could carry stress marking in the transcription. Not found online.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa, Kementerian Pendidikan Dasar dan Menengah. Peta Bahasa: 'Bahasa Balantak, Provinsi Sulawesi Tengah' (language-map entry idb=152; the province list has 21 languages and no separate Andio entry).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology at all: locations, dialect division ('dua dialek, yaitu dialek Masama dan dialek Balantak Banggai. Persentase perbedaan antardialek tersebut sebesar 70,25%') and dialectometric distances to Saluan (77.25%) and Bobongko. Pointer value only: the underlying Badan Bahasa dialectometry survey data (Tangeban observation point) would be held by Balai Bahasa Sulawesi Tengah, not online.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Andio language'; Wikipedia (id) 'Bahasa Andio'; Wikidata Q4754487.
sources.note: No phonology section; references are Ethnologue and Andi-Pallawa 2013 only.

sources.citation: Mead, David. 2024. Sulawesi historical linguistics. In Alexander Adelaar & Antoinette Schapper (eds.), The Oxford guide to the Malayo-Polynesian languages of South East Asia, 150-163. Oxford: OUP.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: digital copy at the publisher (paywalled); the linked copy is not accessible
sources.note: Comparative-historical chapter; most recent expert treatment of the Saluan-Banggai group (Glottolog cites p.154 for Andio). Oxford Guide chapters sometimes summarise prosodic typology, though the Andio-specific content is probably classificatory only.

sources.citation: Any Tadulako University thesis/dissertation by Baso Andi-Pallawa or students on Andio phonology or morphology (the 2013 AJIS article is a spin-off of local-content research at Tadulako University, Palu).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only modern linguist working on Andio; a companion phonology ('Fonologi bahasa Andio') may exist in the Untad repository.

sources.citation: Wumbu, Indra B., Amir Kadir, Nooral Baso & Ny. Sy. Maranua. 1986. Inventarisasi bahasa daerah di propinsi Sulawesi Tengah. Jakarta: Proyek Penelitian Bahasa dan Sastra Indonesia dan Daerah Sulawesi Tengah, Depdikbud. 192 pp.

sources.note: Province-wide inventory of Central Sulawesi languages (Indonesian); Pusat Bahasa inventories sometimes include a short phonological sketch per language. Probably digitised on the Kemdikbud/Kemendikdasmen repository, which was could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid andi1257 (and reference records 7654 Mead 2003; 696534 Mead, David. 2024. Sulawesi historical linguistics. In Adelaar & Schapper (eds.), The Oxford guide to the Malayo-Polynesian languages of South East Asia, 150-163. OUP; 569683 ElCat 2022).

sources.note: Glottolog lists zero descriptive references for Andio; Mead 2024 is cited only for subclassification (p.154) and is paywalled (OUP), not opened.

sources.citation: McConvell, William [Billy]. [2023]. A case for Greater Celebic. Unpublished manuscript, Australian National University; posted on ResearchGate (publication 368282246). Cites Andio' forms (e.g. for a three-way final-nasal distinction). Local press (banggairaya.id 21 Sept 2022; banggainews.com) reports McConvell has researched Andio (Taugi, Tangeban, Serese) for about six years and presented at the Dikbud Banggai seminar 'Struktur Bahasa Andio' -- no publication, thesis or archive deposit from that fieldwork is named anywhere.
